Ship repair | revenue = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|5410.52|c}} (2025)[https://grse.in/financial-results/Q4%20&%20FY%202024-25%20Financial%20Results%20-%20GRSE%20(1).pdf "Financial Report FY25"][https://www.grse.in/annual-reports/Annual_Report_2023_24_English.pdf "Annual Report 23-24"]. | operating_income = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|703.28|c}} (2025) | net_income = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|527.4|c}} (2025 | assets = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|10554.23|c}} (2025) | equity = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|1673.43|c}} (2024) | num_employees = {{decrease}} 1645 (March 2024) | divisions = | website = {{URL|http://www.grse.in}} | footnotes = | intl = | founded = {{start date and age|1884}} | hq_location_city = [[Garden Reach]], [[Kolkata]], [[West Bengal]] | hq_location_country = [[India]] | caption = }} '''Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Ltd''', abbreviated as '''GRSE''', is an Indian [[Defense industry|defence]] [[shipyard]], located in [[Kolkata]].{{cite news|url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/third-antisubmarine-warfare-corvette-launched-in-kolkata/article4551845.ece?homepage=true |title=Third anti-submarine warfare corvette launched in Kolkata |work=The Hindu |first=Vinay |last=Kumar |date=27 March 2013 |access-date=21 February 2015}} It builds and repairs [[merchant shipping|commercial]] and [[warship|naval]] vessels.{{cite web|url=http://www.globalsecurity.org/military/world/india/grse.htm|date = 9 July 2011|title=Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE) |publisher = GlobalSecurity.org |access-date=21 February 2015}} GRSE also exports the ships that the company builds. Founded in 1884 as a small privately owned company on the eastern bank of the [[Hooghly River]], it was renamed as ''Garden Reach Workshop'' in 1916. GRSE was nationalised by the [[Government of India]] in 1960.{{cite news|title=Historical Background|publisher=Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Limited|url=http://www.grse.in/index.php/our-company/historical-background.html|access-date=29 March 2021}} The company was awarded the Miniratna [[Public sector undertakings|public sector undertaking]] status, with accompanying financial and operational autonomy in September 2006.{{cite web|url=http://india.gov.in/sectors/transport/shipping_corp.php?pg=2 |title=Shipping Corporation of India |publisher=india.gov.in |access-date=9 September 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090422231306/http://india.gov.in/sectors/transport/shipping_corp.php?pg=2 |archive-date=22 April 2009 }} GRSE is the first Indian shipyard to build 100 warships.{{Cite web|url=http://www.defencenews.in/article/GRSE-to-be-first-shipyard-in-India-to-make-100-warships-39250|title=GRSE to be first shipyard in India to make 100 warships|website=www.defencenews.in|access-date=2016-11-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161118101037/http://www.defencenews.in/article/GRSE-to-be-first-shipyard-in-India-to-make-100-warships-39250|archive-date=18 November 2016|url-status=dead}} In January 2026, the Department of Defence Production, [[Ministry of Defence (India)|Ministry of Defence]], forwarded a proposal to the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE), [[Ministry of Finance (India)|Ministry of Finance]], seeking an upgrad of GRSE's PSU status to Navratna. The proposal was approved by an inter-ministerial committee in the second week of February and would be placed before an apex committee for final approval.{{Cite news |last=Shukla |first=Anuradha |date=2026-02-19 |title=Garden Reach Shipbuilders set for Navratna status as DPE clears proposal, final nod awaited |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/shipping-/-transport/garden-reach-shipbuilders-set-for-navratna-status-as-dpe-clears-proposal-final-nod-awaited/articleshow/128571774.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2026-02-20 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} ==Facilities== GRSE has ship building facilities in Kolkata and a [[Diesel engine|diesel engine plant]] in [[Ranchi]]. It has a large [[Computer Aided Design|computer-aided design]] (CAD) centre for ship modelling and design. There are four workshops for plate preparation and steel fabrication. GRSE has a [[dry dock]] for ships up to {{DWT|26,000|metric|disp=long}}. It has a building berth and two slipways for [[hull (watercraft)|hull]] construction. It has a covered all-weather non-tidal wet basin for [[fitting-out]] medium and small ships and another fitting-out complex for ships with three [[Berth (moorings)|berth]]s alongside. In addition, it has two river [[jetty|jetties]] for berthing smaller vessels up to {{convert|60|m|ft}} in length. GRSE has engine assemble, test, repair, and overhaul facilities in Ranchi, which acquires 62 acres of land.{{Cite web |title=Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers LTD.- Diesel Engine Plant Ranchi |url=https://grse.in/diesel-engine-plant-ranchi/ |access-date=2024-08-18 |website=grse.in}} GRSE and Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port, Kolkata (SMPK) have inked a long-term concession agreement for GRSE to operate 3 dry docks. Here, GRSE undertakes multiple dry dock repairs of ships up to 160 m length, 20 m beam, and 7 m [[Draft (hull)|draught]]. These docks are situated inside a wet basin, which allows for docking and undocking operations independent of river tidal requirements. The wet basin also has multiple berthing facilities for afloat maintenance and refit operations.{{Cite web |title=Taratala Unit - Official website of Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers Limited – A Government of India undertaking, Ministry of Defence |url=https://grse.in/taratala-unit/index.php |access-date=2024-08-18 |website=grse.in}} On 1 July 2006, GRSE acquired the loss-making Rajabagan Dockyard (RBD) of Central Inland Water Transport Corporation (CIWTC). RBD's facilities with its {{convert|600|m}} waterfront helped alleviate some of GRSE's space constraints and increase its production capacity.{{cite news|url=http://www.business-standard.com/india/news/grse-takes-over-rajabagan-dockyardciwtc/251347/|title=GRSE takes over Rajabagan Dockyard of CIWTC|work =Business Standard|date=11 July 2006|access-date=21 February 2015}} As of 2011, the shipyard was undergoing a {{INRconvert|530|c}} upgrade programme, expected to be completed by March 2012.{{cite web|url=http://www.grse.nic.in/CHAIRMAN'S%20STATEMENT.PDF |title=Annual Report 2010-11 |publisher=Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Limited |access-date=9 September 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110809083834/http://www.grse.nic.in/Chairman%27s%20statement.pdf |archive-date= 9 August 2011 }} The second phase of the upgrade programme was scheduled to commence from June 2013.{{cite web|url=http://www.grse.nic.in/page_aboutus.php?page_id=128 |title=About Us |publisher=Garden Reach Shipbuilders |access-date=21 February 2015}} On 30 January 2024, GRSE signed a Frame and Individual License Agreement with [[Rolls-Royce Power Systems|Rolls-Royce Solutions]], Germany, to cooperate in the [[licensed production]] and localisation of the [[MTU Friedrichshafen|MTU]] IMO Tier II compliant Series 4000 Marine Engines for governmental ships. The agreement enabled GRSE to manufacture the engines in its Diesel Engine Plant in [[Ranchi]]. The engines can power warships of fast [[patrol vessel]], interceptor boat and [[fast attack craft]] class ships of the [[Indian Navy]] and the [[Indian Coast Guard]]. It is already deployed on the [[Car Nicobar-class patrol vessel]]. The series of engines have power output range of {{Convert|746-4300|kW|abbr=on}}. The agreement includes [[Transfer of Technology|transfer of technology]] for engine assembly, painting, parts sourcing, and after-sales service for these engines.{{Cite news |date=2024-01-30 |title=GRSE, Rolls-Royce sign license agreement to manufacture MTU S4000 govt marine engines in India |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/defence/grse-rolls-royce-sign-license-agreement-to-manufacture-mtu-s4000-govt-marine-engines-in-india/articleshow/107267995.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-03-14 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}{{Cite news |last=Peri |first=Dinakar |date=2025-02-17 |title=Offering to co-develop and co-design jet engine, allowing India to own the IP: Rolls Royce |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/offering-to-co-develop-and-co-design-jet-engine-allowing-india-to-own-the-ip-rolls-royce/article69230999.ece |access-date=2025-03-14 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}{{Cite web |title=Series 4000 – power in versatility |url=https://www.rolls-royce.com/media/our-stories/discover/2023/series-4000-power-in-versatility.aspx |access-date=2025-03-14 |website=www.rolls-royce.com |language=en}} On 28 January 2023, a [[Memorandum of Understanding]] (MoU) had also been signed for the same purpose.{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2023-01-28 |title=GRSE signs MoU to manufacture Rolls Royce marine engines in India |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/grse-signs-mou-to-manufacture-rolls-royce-marine-engines-in-india/article66443766.ece |access-date=2025-03-14 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}} ==Vessels built== ===Commercial vessels=== Among commercial and scientific ships, GRSE builds [[oceanography|oceanographic]] and [[hydrographic survey|hydrographic]] [[research vessel]]s, [[Acoustical oceanography|marine acoustic]] research ships, non-propelled [[dredger]]s, grab hopper dredgers, trailing suction hopper dredgers, [[tugboats]], and [[bulk carrier]]s. On 16 July 2024, GRSE signed a contract with the [[National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research]] (NCPOR), [[Ministry of Earth Sciences]], [[Government of India]], for construction of an advanced Ocean Research Vessel (ORV).{{Cite web |title=GRSE secures Rs 491 crore contract from NPOL for Acoustic Research Vessel |url=https://www.psuconnect.in/news/grse-secures-rs-491-crore-contract-from-npol-for-acoustic-research-vessel/44966 |access-date=2024-10-31 |website=www.psuconnect.in |date=31 October 2024 |language=en}} On 29 October 2024, the [[Naval Physical and Oceanographic Laboratory]] (NPOL), an organization under the [[DRDO]], placed an order for a new Acoustic Research Ship (ARS) with the Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers, [[Kolkata]]. The order worth {{INRConvert|490.98|c|lk=on|year=2024}} was signed in [[Kochi]]. The ARS will have an overall length of {{Convert|90|m|ft|abbr=on}} and a beam of {{Convert|14|m|ft|abbr=on}}. It will be able to achieve speeds ranging up to {{Convert|12|kn||abbr=on}}. The ship will have a minimum endurance of 30 days or {{Convert|4500|nmi||abbr=on}}. It will have a complement of 70 personnel. The vessel will have [[diesel-electric propulsion]] and 3 [[deck crane]]s will be fitted on board to handle research equipment. The ARS will be able to deploy, tow, and retrieve a variety of equipment, including acoustic modules; conduct high-resolution surveys of sound velocity profiles in time and/or space; and gather data on ocean tides and currents for use in survey optimisation, underwater mooring design, and offshore deployments. Additionally, it will be able to launch, moor, and maintain independent [[sonobuoys]] as well as gather data from them. The ship will be able to conduct acoustic system experiments at various speed regimes while remaining silent due to its broad speed range. The ARS will also be equipped with a [[dynamic positioning system]] that will enable it to hold its place until [[Sea state|Sea State 4]]. The [[keel laying]] of the ship was conducted on 15 October 2025, with delivery expected in 2027. Being the first silent-class ship to be built in India, it will be capable of deploying and towing various equipment such as acoustic modules, generating sound velocity profiles, collecting ocean data, underwater moored systems, and other facilities for various sea trials.{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2025-10-15 |title=Keel laid for acoustic research ship |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/kerala/keel-laid-for-acoustic-research-ship/article70168006.ece |access-date=2025-10-16 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}} On 2 June 2025, GRSE signed a [[Memorandum of Understanding]] (MoU) with a Norweign firm [[Kongsberg Gruppen|Kongsberg]] in [[Oslo]] for the development of India's first [[Research vessel#Polar research|Polar Research Vessel]] (PRV). This is expected to meet the requirements of [[National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research]] (NCOPR). In 2023, [[Union Minister]] [[Kiren Rijiju]] had informed the [[Rajya Sabha]] that India's first Polar Research Vessel (PRV) was expected to be developed within five years, at an estimated cost of {{INRConvert|2600|c|lk=|year=2023}}.{{Cite news |date=2025-06-03 |title=India to build first-ever indigenous Polar Research Vessel as GRSE signs MoU with Norway's Kongsberg |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/india-to-build-first-ever-indigenous-polar-research-vessel-as-grse-signs-mou-with-norways-kongsberg-101748955355764.html |archive-date= |access-date=2025-06-18 |work=[[Hindustan Times]]}}{{Cite web |date=2025-06-04 |title=Garden Reach inks pact with Norway firm, India to build its first polar research vehicle |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/india/garden-reach-inks-pact-with-norway-firm-india-to-build-its-first-polar-research-vehicle-10046884/ |access-date=2025-06-18 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}} On 11 June 2025, GRSE signed a contract for 2 Coastal Research Vessel (CRV) from the [[Geological Survey of India]]. Each CRV will be {{Convert|64|m||abbr=on}} long and {{Convert|12|m||abbr=on}} wide, with a [[deadweight tonnage]] of around 450 tonnes. Built for extended missions, these vessels will feature an endurance of 15 days and a maximum speed of 10 knots. They will be capable of accommodating up to 35 personnel onboard. The vessels — to be equipped with laboratories for data processing and sample analysis — will be capable of multiple roles like geological mapping, mineral exploration, ocean environment monitoring, and scientific research. The vessels will be powered by diesel electric propulsion and will feature a [[Dynamic positioning|dynamic positioning system]] for operations in [[Sea state|Sea State 3]] conditions.{{Cite web |date=2025-06-11 |title=GRSE shares slip 4% despite signing contract to build 2 coastal research vessels - BusinessToday |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/grse-shares-slip-4-despite-signing-contract-to-build-2-coastal-research-vessels-479933-2025-06-11 |access-date=2025-06-13 |website=Business Today |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=GRSE to Build 2 Coastal Research Vessels for GSI |url=https://www.constructionworld.in/transport-infrastructure/ports-and-shipping/grse-to-build-2-coastal-research-vessels-for-gsi/74988 |access-date=2025-06-13 |website=www.constructionworld.in |language=en}}{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2025-06-03 |title=India to build first indigenous Polar Research Vessel with Norway's Kongsberg |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/economy/logistics/india-to-develop-its-first-ever-polar-research-vessel-in-partnership-with-norway/article69653133.ece |access-date=2025-06-18 |website=BusinessLine |language=en}} As of September 2025, the shipyard is constructing 26 commercial vessels, of which nine are meant for export.{{Cite tweet |number=1966783567620718838 |user=OfficialGRSE |title=GRSE Adds Greater Punch To Navy’s Shallow Water Anti-Submarine Capability, Delivers Second ASW SWC With Indigenous Naval Surface Gun... |date=2025-09-13 |access-date=2025-09-14}} ===Naval vessels=== [[File:Launching of Yard 2095 (3).jpg|thumb|right|Launching ceremonyn, ing Craft Utility (LCU) Mk IV project, 23 Mar 2011.]]By November 2016, GRSE had delivered 98 ships to the Indian Armed Forces. As of March 2024, GRSE has designed and built 108 warships and patrol vessels for the [[Indian Navy]] and the [[Indian Coast Guard|Coast Guard]] for the last 63 years.{{Cite web |last= |date=2024-03-13 |title=GRSE to deliver first advanced guided missile frigate by mid-2025 |url=https://www.lokmattimes.com/national/grse-to-deliver-first-advanced-guided-missile-frigate-by-mid-2025/ |access-date=2024-03-15 |website=Lokmat Times |language=en}} Vessels built at GRSE include [[Frigate#Modern frigate|guided-missile frigates]], [[corvette]]s, [[fleet tanker]]s, [[Fast Attack Craft|fast patrol vessels]], [[amphibious warfare]] vessels and [[hovercraft]]. The 100th ship to be built by the shipyard, LCU L-56 from the [[Mk. IV LCU]] was delivered to the Indian Navy on 30 March 2019.{{Cite press release |title=Induction of in LCU L-56 in the Navy |date=2019-03-30 |publisher=[[Press Information Bureau]] |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1569880®=3&lang=1 |access-date=2026-01-06}} It was the first instance on 30 March 2026 when GRSE delivered three warships to the Indian Navy simultaneously. The triplet included {{INS|Sanshodhak}}, a {{Sclass|Sandhayak|survey vessel|1|5=2023}}; {{INS|Dunagiri|2022|6}}, a {{Sclass|Nilgiri|frigate|1|5=2019}}; and {{INS|Agray|2024|6}}, an [[Anti-Submarine As of September 2025, 13 warships for the Indian Navy are under construction in the shipyard. This includes six [[Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft]], two {{Sclass|Nilgiri|frigate|1||2019}}, four [[Next-Generation Offshore Patrol Vessel|Next Generation Offshore Patrol Vessels]], and one [[Sandhayak-class survey vessel (2023)|Sandhayak-class survey vessel]]. Another contract for five [[Next generation corvette|Next Generation Corvettes]] is expected to be finalised this [[fiscal year]]. GRSE also undertakes ship refitting operations. Some of the notable projects of the Ship Repair Division of GRSE includes: – * [[Abhay-class corvette]] ([[Indian Navy]]) * [[Sri Lanka Navy|Sri Lankan Navy]] Offshore Patrol Vessel * [[MCGS Barracuda]] ([[Mauritius Police Force#National Coast Guard|Mauritius Coast Guard]]) * [[Rajshree-class patrol vessel|PS Zoroaster]] ([[Seychelles Coast Guard]]); twice in 2024{{Cite web |date=2024-06-18|title=INS SUNAYNA IN PORT VICTORIA, SEYCHELLES|url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2026190|access-date=2024-06-18|website=pib.gov.in}} and 2026.{{Cite news |date=2026-02-09 |title=GRSE secures Rs 33-cr MEA order for Seychelles coast guard ship refit |url=https://www.business-standard.com/markets/capital-market-news/grse-secures-rs-33-cr-mea-order-for-seychelles-coast-guard-ship-refit-126020900102_1.html |access-date=2026-02-09 |work=[[Business Standard]]}} * [[Indian Coast Guard]] Ships [[Sarojini Naidu-class patrol vessel|Sarojini Naidu]], [[Samarth-class offshore patrol vessel|Sujay]], [[Vikram-class offshore patrol vessel (2017)|Vijaya]], [[Priyadarshini-class patrol vessel|Priyadarshini]] & [[Sankalp-class offshore patrol vessel|Sankalp]] * SMPK vessels PV Ma Ganga & CV Mahabahu In August 2024, GRSE was undertaking 7 ICG and 2 SMPK vessel refit. ===Exports=== [[File:MCGS Barracuda at sea.jpg|thumb|MCGS ''[[MCGS Barracuda|Barracuda]]'' at sea during delivery]] GRSE delivered the corvette {{ship|MCGS|Barracuda||2}} to Mauritius on 20 December 2014. The contract was worth $58.5 million.{{Cite news |url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/india-to-deliver-corvette-class-warship-to-mauritius-on-december-20/articleshow/45564033.cms |title=India to deliver corvette class warship to Mauritius on December 20 |journal=The Economic Times | date=18 December 2014 | access-date=21 February 2015 }} The Mauritius offshore patrol vessel has an integrated bridge system and can support 83 member crew. It measures {{convert|74.10|m|ft}} in length and {{convert|11.40|m|ft}} in breadth and will be capable of moving at a maximum speed of {{convert|22|kn|km/h}} with an approximate displacement of 1,350 tonnes. GRSE has been short-listed for a patrol boat project for [[Vietnam]] worth {{INRconvert|600|c}} and is also bidding for an order of two frigates for [[Philippines]].{{cite web|url=http://www.affairscloud.com/mcgs-barracuda-first-indias-warship-export-mauritius/ |title=MCGS Barracuda-First India's warship export to Mauritius |publisher=Affairscloud |date=18 December 2014 |access-date=21 February 2015}} GRSE was reported to be the lowest bidder to supply two light frigates to the [[Philippines]]. A total of four firms joined the bidding for the [[Philippine Navy]] project: GRSE; [[Hyundai Heavy Industries]] Inc. and [[Daewoo Shipbuilding & Marine Engineering]] Co. Ltd., both from [[South Korea]]; and [[Navantia]] S.A. of [[Spain]]. GRSE's light frigate would have been a design based on the [[Indian Navy]]'s {{Sclass|Kamorta|corvette}}.{{Cite web |last=Raghuvanshi |first=Vivek |date=2016-05-12 |title=GRSE to Export Light Frigates to Philippines |url=https://www.defensenews.com/global/asia-pacific/2016/05/12/grse-to-export-light-frigates-to-philippines/ |url-status= |archive-url= |archive-date= |access-date=2026-02-25 |website=Defense News |language=en}}{{cite web | url=https://idsa.in/idsacomments/building-frigates-ffor-the-philippines-navy_asaberwal_060716 | title=Building Frigates for the Philippines Navy | Manohar Parrikar Institute for Defence Studies and Analyses }} On 22 June 2024, GRSE secured a contract for the design, construction and delivery of four [[Multi-purpose vessel|multi-purpose vessels]] (MPV) to transport [[windmill]] blades. The deal was signed by ''[[Carsten Rehder|Carsten Rehder Schiffsmakler and Reederei]]'', a German shipbroker and shipowner firm and GRSE for a value of $54 million. The vessels, with a [[deadweight tonnage]] or cargo capacity of 7,500 [[metric tonnes]], will measure 120 metres in length and 17 metres in width with a maximum draught of 6.75 metres. The ships will have a single, large [[cargo hold]] compartment capable of accommodating bulk, general, and project cargoes. Additionally, they will also be capable of carrying [[Cargo containers|containers]] or [[windmill blade]]s on the hatch covers.{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=Benzinga India |title=Garden Reach Shipbuilders Bags ₹448 Cr Export Order From German Company |url=https://in.benzinga.com/content/39444569/garden-reach-shipbuilders-bags-448-cr-export-order-from-german-company |access-date=2024-06-22 |website=Benzinga |language=English}}{{Cite web |title=GRSE share price: GRSE secures export order worth $54 mn from German co for commercial vessels - The Economic Times |url=https://m.economictimes.com/news/defence/grse-secures-export-order-worth-54-mn-from-german-co-for-commercial-vessels/articleshow/111190516.cms |access-date=2024-06-22 |website=m.economictimes.com |date=22 June 2024 }} GRSE has also secured an order of additional 4 MPVs under the "[[Option contract|Option Agreement]]". This brings the total order value of $108 million for 8 ships.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2024-09-06 |title=GRSE bags export order for 4 more commercial vessels |url=https://psuwatch.com/defencewatch/grse-bags-export-order-for-4-more-commercial-vessels |access-date=2024-09-18 |website=PSU Watch |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2024-09-18 |title=GRSE wins order for multi-purpose vessels of 7500 DWT |url=https://www.business-standard.com/amp/markets/capital-market-news/grse-wins-order-for-multi-purpose-vessels-of-7500-dwt-124091801143_1.html |access-date=2024-09-18 |website=Business Standard}} The contract for the construction and delivery of 5th ship was signed on 3 October 2024.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2024-10-07 |title=GRSE signs contract for 5th of 08 multi-purpose Export Vessels |url=https://psuwatch.com/defencewatch/grse-signs-contract-for-5th-of-08-multi-purpose-export-vessels |access-date=2024-10-04 |website=PSU Watch |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=Benzinga India |title=GRSE Inks Contract For 5th Export Vessel With German Client |url=https://in.benzinga.com/markets/equities/24/10/41178197/grse-inks-contract-for-5th-export-vessel-with-german-client |access-date=2024-10-04 |website=Benzinga |language=English}} The final contracts, including those for the seventh and eight vessels, were signed on 24 March 2025. The [[steel cutting]] ceremony for the first vessel of the CORAL 7500 DWT MPV series was held on 17 April 2025. The project is undertaken in coordination with multiple firms including F.H. Bertling, ForestWave Navigation/Schulte & Bruns, and Delft Shipping. Meanwhile, M/s SEDS and [[DNV]] are the designing partner and the agency for classification and certification, respectively. ForestWave will serve as the time chartered for the first and fifth vessel, named CORAL STRAIT and CADIZ STRAIT, respectively. This is Carsten Rehder's first project in India.{{Cite web |date=2025-04-17 |title=GRSE Commences Production of Multi Purpose Vessel Project |url=https://www.psuconnect.in/psu-news/grse-commences-production-of-multi-purpose-vessel-project |access-date=2025-09-22 |website=www.psuconnect.in |language=en}}{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2025-04-17 |title=GRSE commences construction of Multipurpose Vessels for German firm Carsten Rehder |url=https://psuwatch.com/defencewatch/grse-commences-construction-of-multipurpose-vessels-for-german-firm-carsten-rehder |access-date=2025-09-22 |website=PSU Watch |language=en}} On 1 July 2024, GRSE received another $21 million order for a 800-tonne Advanced [[Ocean-going tug|Ocean-Going Tug]] from the [[Bangladesh Navy]]. The tugboat will be delivered within 24 months of signing the contract. The tugboat is expected to measure 61 meters in length, about 15.80 meters in width and have a draught of nearly 6.80 meters. The order was received a few weeks after receiving an order for a [[trailing suction hopper dredger]] (TSHD). GRSE also has an order of 6 patrol boats for the Bangladesh's [[Department of Fisheries (Bangladesh)|Department of Fisheries]].{{Cite web |date=2024-07-01 |title=Garden Reach Shipbuilders wins $21 million order; Stock surges to take market cap past ₹25,000 crore - CNBC TV18 |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/garden-reach-shipbuilders-21-million-order-win-bangladesh-contract-market-cap-25000-crore-19436136.htm |access-date=2024-07-01 |website=CNBCTV18 |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2024-07-01 |title=India's GRSE inks deal with Bangladesh Navy under $500-mn line of credit |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/indias-grse-inks-deal-with-bangladesh-navy-under-500-mn-line-of-credit-101719835860896.html |access-date=2024-07-03 |website=[[Hindustan Times]]}} On 19 September 2025, Germany's Carsten Rehder placed another order for four Hybrid Multi-Purpose Vessels (MPVs). The contract, worth $62.44 million was signed in [[Hamburg]], Germany and includes an Option Agreement for two more vessels. These Hybrid MPVs will have similar dimensions and cargo capabilities as in the CORAL 7500 DWT MPV series except for the these MPVs will feature battery-assisted hybrid propulsion system with enhanced fuel efficiency. The design will be in line with the [[International Maritime Organization]]’s (IMO) decarbonisation targets.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2025-09-20 |title=GRSE signs $62.44 million contract with Germany's Carsten Rehder for 4 vessels |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/economy/logistics/grse-signs-6244-million-contract-with-germanys-carsten-rehder-for-4-vessels/article70073180.ece |access-date=2025-09-22 |website=BusinessLine |language=en}} The fourth keel was laid on 30 August 2026. The contract was then expanded to 12 vessels making it the largest commercial shipbuilding order ever secured by the firm.{{Cite news |date=2026-05-30 |title=Kolkata-based Defence PSU GRSE lays keel for 4th vessel in German MPV project |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/shipping-/-transport/kolkata-based-defence-psu-grse-lays-keel-for-4th-vessel-in-german-mpv-project/articleshow/131410872.cms |access-date=2026-05-31 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} == See also == * [[List of shipbuilders and shipyards in India]] * [[Cochin Shipyard|Cochin Shipyard Limited, Cochin]] * [[Hooghly Cochin Shipyard Limited|Hooghly Cochin Shipyard Limited, Kolkata]] * [[Titagarh Wagons]], [[West Bengal]] * [[Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders]], [[Mumbai]] * [[Hindustan Shipyard]], [[Visakhapatnam]] * [[Shalimar Works (1980) Ltd|Shalimar Works (1980) Ltd, Howrah]] * [[Goa Shipyard]] * [[Inland Waterways Authority of India]] * [[Kolkata Port|Shyama Prasad Mukerjee Port]], [[Kolkata]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{commons category|Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers}} {{coord|22|32|16.9|N|88|17|48.78|E|scale:5000_region:IN|display=title}} {{Public Sector Undertakings in India}} {{authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers}} [[Category:Shipbuilding companies of India]] [[Category:Diesel engine manufacturers]] [[Category:Marine engine manufacturers]] [[Category:Indian Navy]] [[Category:Government-owned companies of India]] [[Category:Companies nationalised by the Government of India]] [[Category:Engine manufacturers of India]] [[Category:Manufacturing companies based in Kolkata]] [[Category:Indian companies established in 1884]] [[Category:Manufacturing companies established in 1884]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]]

Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Ltd, abbreviated as GRSE, is an Indian defence shipyard, located in Kolkata. It builds and repairs commercial and naval vessels. GRSE also exports the ships that the company builds.
Founded in 1884 as a small privately owned company on the eastern bank of the Hooghly River, it was renamed as Garden Reach Workshop in 1916. GRSE was nationalised by the Government of India in 1960. The company was awarded the Miniratna public sector undertaking status, with accompanying financial and operational autonomy in September 2006. GRSE is the first Indian shipyard to build 100 warships.
In January 2026, the Department of Defence Production, Ministry of Defence, forwarded a proposal to the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE), Ministry of Finance, seeking an upgrad of GRSE's PSU status to Navratna. The proposal was approved by an inter-ministerial committee in the second week of February and would be placed before an apex committee for final approval.
